verses.1: And the LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying:
verses.2: This is the law of the Torah that Jehovah commanded: “Speak to the children of Israel and tell them to bring back to you pure, unblemished livestock. No death shall be allowed upon such livestock.”
verses.3: And you shall give it to Elazar the priest. He shall take it outside the camp and slaughter it before him.
verses.4: And Elazar, the priest, took it from the altar on its sides, and he placed it in front of the altar of the congregation, seven times.
verses.5: And he burned the cow to his eyes: its horn, its flesh, and its blood were all burned on the ground.
verses.6: And the priest took a fig tree and a vineyard, along with two branches, and he threw them into the fire where the crops were being burned.
verses.7: And the priest, with his clothes on, bathed his hands in the water. After that, he went to the tent and washed himself clean until dawn.
verses.8: And the one who burns her will be covered with his clothes in the water. He will wash his body in the water, and he will become unclean until morning.
verses.9: And a clean man gathered the dung of the sheep, and placed it outside the camp, in a place that was clean. It became a reminder for the children of Israel to remember that this was a time for repentance for their sins.
verses.10: And he would collect all the sheep and their wool, and wash them until they were clean. Then they became a law for the children of Israel, and for the foreigners living among them, as a perpetual statute.
verses.11: He who causes death to every human being and to the unclean animals for seven days.
verses.12: He will be defiled on the third day and on the seventh day. If he does not become defiled on the third day and on the seventh day, then he will not be cleansed at all.
verses.13: All those who die in a state of sin, those who do not repent of their sins, their souls will be marked as unclean by God. Their souls will be rejected from Israel, because they have committed evil deeds. They will continue to be unclean forever.
verses.14: This is the Torah: that man shall die in the tent. All those who come to the tent will be buried there for seven days.
verses.15: And everything that has no fastener at the end, where the thread should be attached, is useless.
verses.16: And everything that is killed on the face of the field, in the field of destruction, or when a person dies or when a body is destroyed, shall be buried for seven days.
verses.17: And they took water from the abyss of punishment for sin, and poured it upon him.
verses.18: And Ezov took a clean person and soaked him in water. He then sprinkled this water on the altar, on all the utensils, and on the souls that were there. He also sprinkled it on those who touched the body, whether they were alive or dead.
verses.19: And he was cleansed from his impurity on the third day and on the seventh day. On the seventh day, his sin was forgiven. He washed his clothes and bathed in the water, and thus he became clean.
verses.20: And whoever is unclean and does not wash himself, his soul will be marked among the people. For he has defiled the holiness of Jehovah; he is unclean, and no one should touch him.
verses.21: And it shall be a law for them forever. They shall wrap themselves in their clothes and lie down on the ground. They shall remain there until dawn.
verses.22: And everything that touches it will be covered in dirt. The skin that touches it will also be covered in dirt, until morning comes.
